News.title: Knifeman who ‘sliced woman’s throat’ in Brit tourist hotspot yelled ‘Allah’ before killing her, witnesses say
News.content:
A KNIFEMAN who allegedly stabbed a woman to death in Barcelona shouted “Allahu is great” before the suspected attack, reports say.

It comes after a harrowing image of the knife-wielding assailant prowling the streets just moments after the alleged assault was revealed.





Spanish police have not confirmed the suspect‘s nationality – but local media reports he is Moroccan.

He was reportedly seen acting “nervously” in the moments leading up to the stabbing.

Terrified witnesses claimed he had yelled out “Allah is great” before the alleged assault, El Mundo and Telecinco reported.

Jose Luis, a 58-year-old victim who was injured after confronting the suspect, said: “I heard some shouting and ran up some steps to the area where the noise was coming from.

“I saw what appeared to be the man going for his victim and yelled at him.

“He turned round and came towards me and tried to stab me at the top of the stairs but didn’t manage to.

“That’s when I tried to hit him. He didn’t like that and picked up some stones from the ground.”

He added: “He threw and hit me with them in the arm, and then attempted to stab me three or four times again.”



The hero continued: “It was easier for him to stab a young woman than a man.

“The neighbours started shouting ‘police, police’, and he turned and ran.”

Locals in Esplugues de Llobregat near Barcelona‘s Nou Camp where the 11am stabbing occurred on Saturday said they had seen the suspect in the area in the days leading up to the stabbing.



One resident said it looked like he had been “casing it out”.

He is accused of stabbing the woman multiple times and cutting her throat before fleeing the scene.

Previous reports claimed the victim was a 16-year-old girl.

But police sources have confirmed she was an adult and not a minor.

Her exact age has not been made public yet.



Local cops also say they are still trying to figure out if the attacker was known to the woman.

Esplugues de Llobregat Town Hall said: “We deeply regret the violent death of a person in the town and extend our condolences to their family and loved ones.

“The council condemns all forms of violence and expresses its concern over these serious incidents, which affect community life and public safety.

“The alleged perpetrator has already been arrested by the Mossos d’Esquadra regional police force.

“From the outset, the Council has been coordinating with the Mossos d’Esquadra, the force leading the investigation, and the Esplugues Local Police, and is offering all necessary institutional cooperation to help clarify the facts.”

They also said two days of official mourning had started.

News.title: Meet Britain’s newest dog breeds – including revived 90s Russian pup officially granted recognition by The Kennel Club
News.content:
FROM Labradors to a bichon frise, the UK is home to hundreds of loveable dog breeds.

And now, two more pooches have been added to the list, bringing the total to 227.





The Kennel Club has officially recognised the Miniature American Shepherd and Yakutian Laika as dog breeds in the UK.

While the Miniature American Shepherd originates from the US, the Yakutian Laika comes from Siberia.

The miniature American Shepherd is a small herding breed, known for its high intelligence, agility, and loyalty.

It was first recognised by the American Kennel Club in 2011 and by the Fédération Cynologique Internationale (FCI) in 2019.



Since then, the breed has been becoming increasingly established in the UK.

Meanwhile, the Yakutian Laika was bred as a working canine, primarily employed as a sled dog.

This breed is celebrated for its resilience, instinct, and unwavering devotion.

“Rooted in the vast and demanding landscape of northeastern Russia, the Yakutian Laika is an ancient working breed shaped over millennia by its vital role in transport, hunting and daily survival,” the Kennel Club said.



The breed was revived in the 1990s and formally recognised by the Russian Kynological Federation in 2004.

“Today, the Yakutian Laika stands as a striking, versatile companion whose popularity is steadily rising worldwide,” the Kennel Club added.

From July 1, the Kennel Club will recognise both these “breeds of pedigree dog”, meaning it has traceable ancestry going back several generations on both sides.

Pedigree dogs are predictable in terms of their temperament and physical appearance as well as their exercise, grooming, and general care needs.

The last breed to be recognised by the Kennel Club was the Hungarian Mudi in July 2025.



Previous recognition also include the Icelandic Sheepdog in 2025, the Polish Hunting Dog in 2024, the Smooth Faced Pyrenean Sheepdog in 2021, and the Barbet in 2020.

News.title: Paranoid Putin ‘hides in bunkers for WEEKS over coup fears’ as Ukraine drone hits Moscow days before Victory Day parade
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin has been hiding in bunkers for weeks over fears he will be toppled, reports say – as Ukraine struck a Moscow apartment days before a major military parade.

The paranoid Russian tyrant has retreated to an underground unit – and security has been massively ramped amid mounting speculation of a coup.





On Monday, a Ukrainian drone hit a luxury high-rise apartment in Moscow – a rare blow to the Kremlin dictator’s well-protected capital city.

Images showed a gaping hole punched into the side of the building following the blast which caused no injuries.

The strike came on the third night in a row of consecutive Ukrainian drone assaults – which come just days before a scaled-back parade on May 9.

The Victory Day event will mark the Soviet Union’s victory over Nazi Germany.



Putin is said to be working “for weeks” on end in secret bunkers over concerns he is the target of a simmering coup.

According to Russian outlet Important Stories, Western intelligence has reported high-level Kremlin panic over an imminent power grab.



Since the beginning of March 2026, Moscow has been looking over its shoulder amid growing reports of an upcoming plot to oust Putin.

The despot is said to be fearing a drone-led assassination orchestrated by top-ranking Russian officials, reports say.

His Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu is alleged to be part of the reported plot.



Shoigu was first linked to coup fears last month when his former deputy Ruslan Tsalikov was arrested over suspected corruption.

The claims of Putin paranoia are based on the analysis of an intelligence agency of a European Union country which was not named.

The pariah has significantly tightened security measures, the report adds.



Personnel working near Putin have been banned from using mobile phones or taking public transport.

Visits to the Russian president now require two levels of screening and a full body search, it claims.

Putin is also making a lot fewer public appearances – while the list of locations regularly attended also cut down.

He reportedly lives with his glamorous Olympic gymnast partner Alina Kabaeva, 42, and their sons Ivan, 11, and Vladimir, six.

The children use the family name Spiridonov.



He is said to be hiding in his £1billion clifftop Gelendzhik palace, equipped with multiple underground floors.

The fortress has been likened to the lair of a James Bond villain.

He has not visited his usual residences in Moscow or his tightly guarded Valdai palace.

The latest Ukrainian drone strike has also sparked fresh fears for Putin’s leadership – with the dictator now imposing a sweeping security clampdown.

The Kremlin is quaking in its boots over worries Ukraine will attack rehearsals for the showpiece – or the main event itself.



Putin is due to make a “very important” speech at the parade – with fears he could be targeted.

Snipers and machine gunners have appeared on towers near the Kremlin, which overlooks Red Square, local media reported.

Armoured vehicles and trucks with anti-drone weapons are being deployed at the Kremlin.

News.title: Inside country where girls as young as 6 are burned alive for being ‘witches’ as survivor’s terrifying escape revealed
News.content:
A SEETHING mob crowds around a young mum doused in gasoline as she is thrown into blazing pit and burned alive after being accused of using black magic.

It sounds like a medieval tale from ages past – but it is one of thousands of witch hunt cases which still happen to this day, and the phenomenon is getting worse.





The victim, mum-of-two Kepari Leniata, 20, was stripped, bound and covered in petrol by neighbours who accused her of using sorcery to kill their six-year-old boy in Papua New Guinea.

The horrifying 2013 killing sparked outrage – forcing authorities to revoke a law that allowed sorcery accusations to be used as a defence in murder cases.

But over a decade later, sorcery accusation related violence often called witch hunts, are still commonplace.

It’s often women who face torture, sexual assault, and threats after being accused of using sorcery.



Some victims are even forced to abandon their homes and live in exile.

When Monica Paulus’ father died from a heart attack in 2003, she was accused of being behind his death by her own brother.

Her sibling – a local pastor – labelled her a witch, or “sanguma”, before people in the community threatened to kill or torture her.

The human rights activist told The Sun how she was forced to flee her hometown due to the threats.



Monica told us: “There is nothing you will say for people to listen to you.

“And to make it worse, it’s not anyone outside, it’s somebody that is your immediate family.

“It’s your brother who’s saying it, and I was helpless.”



She added: “I was crushed, as if I was gonna die at that moment.”

Miranda Forsyth, the director of the International Network Against Accusations of Witchcraft and Associated Harmful Practices, said women can face horrifying torture or death when they are accused.

She said: “The women who are accused are subjected to sometimes having burning irons inserted, they have their breasts cut.

“They’re left with these permanent injuries, or else they’re killed.

“And men will typically have their limbs cut off. They might be left without a hand or without a leg, and obviously the risk of bleeding to death then is very high as well.”



The expert branded these cases “really extreme forms of human rights abuse”.

After fleeing to another province while fearing for her life, Monica claims she witnessed another victim being stoned to death after resisting rape.

She said the woman had been suspected of using black magic after she bit the tongue of the man trying to sexually assault her.



Watching in sheer horror as the accused woman was being killed, Monica said she stood helplessly thinking: “I will never survive.”

She described being branded a sanguma as a “life sentence”.

“You’re always looking over your back, behind your shoulder to make sure no one’s coming to get you,” Monica said.

“Constantly I live in fear.”

Sorcery-related violence may sound like an archaic practice, but it’s a “very new phenomenon”, Forsyth said.



At least 20,000 people across 60 countries were accused of witchcraft between 2009 and 2019, according to a 2023 UN report.

Papua New Guinea authorities recorded 16 cases in 2021 – but this soared to 96 in the first nine months of 2024, showing the dramatic increase.

The trend has plagued the Pacific nation with a population of 10 million people – but has notably been recorded at higher frequencies in the Southern Highlands region.

People accuse others of witchcraft for range of reasons, Forsyth explained.

Those pointing the finger may want to disgrace their victims, provoke a conflict, or use it as an excuse to get rid of opponents.



But at its core, accusations of witchcraft often fill the gap when people can’t explain why bad things happen.

“Fundamentally, it’s a way of explaining why misfortunes are occurring,” she said.

“When we see poverty, insecurity, increasing levels of health issues that aren’t able to be addressed by the hospital system, then people do start to ask, why is this occurring?

“And sorcery provides an explanation for it. It is a pervasive and ongoing form of human rights abuse.”

Describing the burden that comes with being accused, Monica said: “You go around with it.



“If anything happens, like if there’s a misfortune, if there is a sickness, if there is an accident, people will still accuse you because you’re going with a tag around.”

Accusations of wielding black magic can often be passed down to offspring, Monica added.

Those seeking to blame a misfortune on someone will often turn their heads to anyone blood-related to suspected sorcerers, she said.

Accusations also often come from within the family – the same way Monica was subject to a witch hunt.

“It’s people that you rely on for safety and people that you look up to,” Monica said.



“You trust them, they are the ones who will attack you.”

Forsyth explained: “It can become an inter-generational problem as well.”

In a haunting twist of fate, 20-year-old Kepari’s six-year-old daughter was reportedly burned with hot knives in 2017 by locals who also accused her of practising sorcery.

“The amount of pain that these victims suffer is extraordinary,” Forsyth said.

Mobs of intoxicated men are known to go on witch hunts, tracking down women, Forsyth said.



In some communities, a traditional “Glassman” checks witchcraft claims by reading smoke from burning bamboo.

Elsewhere, “prayer warriors” blame cases on Satan.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Looking forward, Forsyth said there needs to be stricter regulation and policing across the country.

She said: “If nothing is done to address it, then things are deteriorating… there needs to be a real emphasis on prosecutions.”

News.title: My wife was run over twice by ‘drunk’ driver on holiday in fatal crash… I tried to lift car off her but it was too late
News.content:
IN the kitchen of their Essex family home, Keith Di Palma and his two grown daughters sit at a granite worktop adorned with bright floral bouquets.

With the spring sunshine flooding through the window and a forest of vibrant flowers decorating the house, if someone took a photo, it could look like a celebratory scene. And that’s exactly what it should be. This day marks the 62nd birthday of the beloved wife and mum of the house, Lisa Di Palma. But she’s the one person missing from the picture.





This year, she won’t get to enjoy the flowers sent by well-wishers or receive the traditional birthday hugs from her girls.

Lisa’s life was cut short in an instant when she was mowed down by a “drunk driver” while on holiday in Turkey on August 6 last year – a trip she and Keith had taken to celebrate their 36th wedding anniversary.

On Tuesday, May 5, the alleged driver, Turkish national Senay Koparal, 54, will stand trial for her death.

Witnesses claim the driver attempted to flee the scene and, in doing so, ran her over again.

Koparal is said to have been “five times” over the drink-drive limit when he hit Lisa as she crossed a pedestrian crossing with Keith, 57.

They were on their way to enjoy a meal on the turquoise coastline in Fethiye, in southwestern Turkey, shortly after 7.30pm.

Footage of the horrific incident filmed by passersby shows Keith courageously trying to push the car off his stricken wife’s body.

The clips quickly went viral in the country, and a media frenzy whipped up around the family as their “living nightmare” unravelled.



His hands wrapping a mug of tea, and gazing into a framed picture of smiling Lisa on the wall, Keith says: “It was a holiday in paradise that turned into hell in a matter of minutes.

“Lisa was walking just behind me. We were looking forward to having a nice dinner on the front – the sort of thing all couples do each night when on holiday.

“I was walking slightly ahead of Lisa across the pedestrian crossing, and I felt the car brush my back.

“She had no chance to escape. It hit her straight on. I tried to grab the guy out of the car, but he went forward over her again.”

The brutal footage was spread by Turkish news channels and social media groups shows Keith standing in front of the car as he grips the bonnet, desperately trying to push the vehicle off his wife. Three other men heroically rushed to help shove the car back.



Eyes brimming with tears, Keith went on: “Once he had finally stopped, I tried to get the keys out of the car. One of the men who was helping said, ‘Go to your wife. We will stop him.’

“He [Koparal] was trying to get away, but he didn’t really seem to know what was going on.

“Once they got him out of the car, he just lit a cigarette. How could anyone do that?

“Lisa was on the road, and there was blood all over her, but she was conscious.”

An ambulance rushed to Lisa as she lay unable to move on the tarmac. The grandma-of-four was rushed to a nearby A&E, where she was “patched up”, before being sent to the larger Mugla University Hospital.



Daughter Danielle, 34, told how her frantic dad called her as he followed the ambulance to the hospital.

She says: “Mum and dad called us every night that they were away, but as soon as I heard my dad’s voice this time, I knew something was wrong.

“He told me about the accident – I got straight on a plane and met them at the hospital. When I got there, I found mum was just left on a stretcher; she didn’t even have a bed. It was awful.



“They did an MRI and an X-ray, then she was moved again to a private hospital.

“We knew she was seriously hurt, but we thought she was going to be okay at that point. She was talking to us – she was asking about the grandkids and the dogs.

“The worst part was we could only see her for five minutes a day, even when she was conscious and talking.

“On the fifth day after the accident, we noticed that her stomach looked very bloated. It looked like she was pregnant. The doctors then explained to us that there was a bowel obstruction.”

Lisa’s younger daughter, Charlotte, 32, also flew out to join the family in Turkey.



Tragically, the day she landed – which was just six days after the incident – the family received the call they had been dreading.

Danielle explains: “The hospital said she had taken a turn for the worse and to get there as fast as we could. At that point, I was sure that we had lost her. I started to have a panic attack because we got there so fast, but no one would tell us what was happening.

“Finally, the doctor came and told us that her heart had stopped for ten minutes, but they had managed to stabilise her. They put her in an induced coma.”



Charlotte says she could tell her mum could hear her as she lay sedated: “She was still moving in response to what we were saying.”

“I know she could hear us. We didn’t want to leave her, but the hospital said we had to.

“We prayed it would be okay, and she just needed to be put into a coma to let her body recover.”

At 4.30am the next morning, they got another call asking them to return as soon as possible.

By the time the family arrived, it was too late. A doctor told how they had tried to revive Lisa for an hour, but despite their best efforts, she had passed away.



The family asked to see her to say their goodbyes.

“What happened then will never leave me,” says Keith. “We wanted time with her to hold her and say bye.

“But they brought her through in a body bag and unzipped it in front of us.

“We had a few minutes, and they just zipped it back up again. I didn’t get to kiss her goodbye. It was awful.”



When news of Lisa’s death leaked to the Turkish press, a media mob rushed to the hospital and the local morgue to try to get a glimpse of the stricken family.

Danielle says: “We had to go to the morgue straight away, even though they wouldn’t let us identify my mum because we were not Turkish. The media were already there. I had cameras in my face. Even inside the morgue, the press were sitting in the waiting room with cameras.

“There is a video of the coffin my mum was in leaving the morgue, which was put out on Turkish TV. We felt completely hounded, and we knew it would not get better.”

Understandably, the family wanted to leave the country as soon as possible and took a flight that day to escape further local media attention.

But footage of the incident that led to their mum’s death was already being shared by thousands over social media sites TikTok, Snapchat and Facebook.



Both Danielle and Charlotte have seen the videos, but Keith refuses to watch them.

The family are worried that one day Lisa’s grandchildren, Alfie, 13, Darcie, eight, Evie, seven and Albie, two, may one day see the awful footage of their much-loved gran, who is now frozen in time on the World Wide Web in that horrific moment.

Charlotte, an insurance worker who is mum to Alfie and Evie, says: “We were in a state of shock and the fact we were having it thrown in our faces all the time when we were over there.

“The press were everywhere, and even people in the hospital were pointing at us.

“There is the worry that our kids will see it now as time goes on. My son is thirteen now, and I do worry about that.



“It is difficult, though, because the video is what led to Koparal facing the most extreme charge – it’s evidence.

“Until that video evidence surfaced, he was going to be done for just drink driving. But the footage shows clearly what happened, and that has helped us in a huge way in terms of us hoping to get justice for our mum.”

The funeral for Lisa, who dedicated her life to helping others and was the secretary of the Tigers Junior Football Club and the Echo Junior Football League for decades, was attended by over 1,000 people.

A foundation has now been set up in her name that has raised £40,000 to help underprivileged kids in their local area in Havering, Essex, have access to youth football, in tribute to her passion.

Keith, who works at Ford Motors, adds: “She was one of the greatest humans on earth.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“She would stay up into the early hours, dedicating her life to youth football and making sure any child who wanted to play could do so.

“She was very loved by so many, and we want her legacy to live on. Which we know it will do.”

News.title: Sick scammer pretending to be my missing girl, 2, is travelling 3,500 miles to meet me – she won’t take no for an answer
News.content:
DAD'S TORMENT Sick scammer pretending to be my missing girl, 2, is travelling 3,500 miles to meet me – she won’t take no for an answer

AN AMERICAN woman says she will come to the UK for a DNA test to prove she is Katrice Lee, the missing daughter of former sergeant major Richard Lee.

Heather McCord founded a GoFundMe page – which has since been taken down – asking the public to help fund the trip that she insists will confirm her connection to the Lee family.





Katrice went missing in Paderborn, Germany, in 1981 on her 2nd birthday. Her family have been searching for answers ever since.

Posting on Facebook, Heather wrote: “I am going over there and I am going to do the DNA test and hand over all the evidence I have weather [sic] people like it or not.”

However Richard said he has no doubts the claims are fake and that she is only exploiting their tragedy to scam the public.

His daughter, Natasha Walker, was the first one in the family to discover the page, after it had been flagged to her through a missing persons group.

“My initial reaction was very angry, and if I could’ve put my hands round their neck to express my anger I would’ve done,” he said, adding that she’d put a “very clever story together”.

“To the person with the untrained eye, her claims seemed plausible.



“But there were red flags, such as being trafficked as a two-year-old child. Who remembers anything from when they were two? I certainly don’t.”

Posting to her TikTok page in November last year, Heather claimed that she’d been told she was abducted as a child.

On her Facebook she added that she had “bits of pieces of memories” of the kidnapping, which she described as “worse than horror movies and nightmares combined”.

She said that the “abduction” had been confirmed to her by “a few law enforcement officers” and that she had the “documentation” to prove it.

Heather claims to have a condition known as “xoforia” (‘exophoria’ being the correct term), where one eye drifts outwards, which she claims confirms she is Katrice.



Katrice suffered from strabismus, a related eye condition which was severe enough it would have needed two operations to correct.

Heather also claims she has an identical birthmark to Katrice’s on her lower back, resembling a rash.

An alleged lack of cooperation from US law enforcement has pushed her to reach out to UK agencies, who she claims are prepared to help.

Her GoFundMe page appeared to have raised $217 before being taken down from multiple platforms.

Heather claimed all of it had been spent on a flight to the UK, attaching a receipt dating to January this year on her Facebook page as proof of purchase.



Richard said his daughter Natasha and ex-wife Sharon had notified the Royal Military Police (RMP) about the fundraiser link.

“I can only assume that the cogs have started to turn and hit home,” said Richard. “Because one of the GoFundMe pages has disappeared.

“This individual’s goal in life is to make as much money on the back of people’s tragedy.”

Responding to the allegations that she is a scammer, Heather wrote: “I understand why the Lee family would feel like I would be a

scammer because of everything they’ve been through.

“I promise I just want to find out who I really am and if it turns out I’m not

Katrice then they will never hear from me again just like they haven’t

heard from me all this time.”



This is not the first time Richard and his family have been contacted by strangers since Katrice went missing.

“There are some people who come forward, who genuinely believe they are Katrice,” he said.

“And if they fall into the bracket, the RMP takes their DNA and checks it out.

“But those people then disappear with dignity. But then you’ve got the other ones, who hang on and make the family’s life a nightmare.

“Why do they do it? My personal opinion is that they’re a whacko, a fruit-and-nut case.”



One of the family’s tormentors was Donna Wright, from County Durham.

She repeatedly harassed them via phone calls in 2014 while on a suspended sentence for the same offence.

“She made comments to Natasha like, ‘Fancy losing your sister over a packet of crisps?’” he said.

Another harasser, Heidi Robinson, pleaded guilty to a malicious communications offence in 2019 and was sentenced to 18 weeks in prison, suspended for two years, with a mental health treatment order.

According to Richard, the entire investigation was a botched job within the first few days of Katrice’s disappearance, including poor communication between the RMP and local authorities.



“I try and be level about it, don’t set my hopes too high and take it one day at a time,” said Richard.

“I’ve been asked, do you believe she’s still alive?

“Yes, I do. I’m a giant and I stand tall. Katrice is definitely alive. I would ask the RMP to prove otherwise.”

A spokesperson for the Defence Serious Crime Command said: “We confirm that we have received information concerning an individual making unfounded claims to be Katrice Lee.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We recognise that claims of this nature are extremely distressing for her family. We urge anyone with new information regarding Katrice’s disappearance to contact the DSCC Major Crime Team on 0800 616 888.”

News.title: Passenger ‘sexually assaulted sleeping woman on flight to Miami & left creepy note behind’
News.content:
A PASSENGER groped a sleeping woman sat beside him on a flight before returning to give her a creepy note, court records say.

Guillaume Sebastien Roger Mattler, 48, has been charged with one count of abusive sexual contact, according to a federal criminal complaint.



He was sat beside a 29-year-old woman in a first-class cabin, according to court documents seen by the New York Post.



As the woman dozed off, the man allegedly tried to move his fingers beneath the victim’s clothing.

The stomach-churning alleged assault was reportedly caught on camera by two horrified passengers on the Swiss International Air Lines Flight LX64 to Miami.

“Witness 2 observed Mattler moving his hand in a ‘submarine’ motion, as if trying to get his hand under the Victim’s clothing and/or between her legs,“ an FBI Special Agent wrote in a statement.

The passenger became “very concerned” and alerted the cabin crew, the statement said.

The witness allegedly saw Mattler with his hand on the stranger’s “crotch, over her jeans, making a scooping or rubbing motion”, the records state.

The woman, who did not know Mattler, had no idea of the alleged assault occurring as she slept, authorities said.

Only when an air hostess told her of the alleged incident did the young woman begin shaking and crying.

In a further sickening twist, the accused returned to his seat and handed the victim a note which said: “You look beautiful when you are sleeping”.



The Frenchman claimed “nothing had happened” on the flight.

When confronted with video evidence, he reportedly confessed that he “touched the woman sitting next to him and that he did not think it was such a big deal”, according to court documents.

He said he he had “only” touched the woman’s lower back and buttocks, the documents claim.

When investigators pointed out that witnesses saw him, he reportedly said that “he touched whatever he could reach from across the armrest”.

Mattler returns to court on Monday after his first hearing last week.



It comes after an air stewardess was reportedly groped mid-flight last month before the shameless perv was dragged off the plane.

The shocking alleged incident left passengers horrified as the man reportedly claimed his actions did not “count as sexual harassment”.

The accused allegedly said he merely “lightly patted” the cabin crew member on the flight from Malaysia to China.

News.title: Woman building beach club in her garden makes colossal mistake with sand
News.content:
Woman building beach club in her garden makes colossal mistake with sand

A woman who is turning her garden into a 'beach club' for the summer put in an order for a large bag of sand for decoration - but made one big mistake that could ruin her plans

View Image The woman made one big mistake with her beach garden transformation (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

Turning your garden into an Ibiza-style beach club might sound like a great idea, but you might want to do your research first. Summer is almost upon us, and as the weather warms up, it's time for Brits to indulge in many of our favourite summer pastimes - like having too many drinks in a pub beer garden or enjoying a barbecue at home.

‌



One woman on social media who wanted to bring the summer vibes to her garden early had a more unique approach, though. Caity Baser decided to turn her garden into a "beach club" reminiscent of holidays in Ibiza, complete with an inflatable swimming pool, palm trees, and masses of sand.

‌



However, in a recent TikTok video updating her followers on the status of her project, it was revealed that Caity had unfortunately made a colossal error when ordering the sand for her garden.

‌



The woman said she had ordered a tonne of sand, and when it was dropped off at the front of her house, she soon realised she wasn't anywhere near strong enough to drag the 1,000kg bag through her home and into her garden. She found herself having to resort to filling up several buckets and making multiple trips.

Caity had laid out a tarpaulin in her garden to protect her grass and dumped the buckets of sand out onto the blue plastic sheet with the intention of completely covering it up.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



But commenters were quick to point out that the less-than-ideal position of the bag wasn't the only mistake she'd made. Even worse than the extra exercise she'd had to do, Caity had ordered builder's sand for her project - not the sand typically seen on a beach.

The sand found on most beaches is known as silica sand or quartz sand, which is composed of silicon dioxide, which forms when hard quartz breaks down over thousands of years of weathering and erosion. While it is found on beaches, it can also be used for golf course bunkers, aquariums, and even equestrian surfaces.

Builder's sand, meanwhile, has a lower salt content, a specific angular grain shape, and a washed consistency. It is better suited to being used as structural mortar and concrete, as it can hold water, and the grains can bond tightly together.

‌



One commenter on Caity's post wrote: "Oh Caity. Why have you got builders' sand?"

Another added: "That's not the same as beach sand, your garden will be a quagmire when it rains."

A third posted: "At least you're gonna get a full beach experience with the sea included after it rains."

Article continues below

Others commented that if there are households with outdoor cats in Caity's area, they will likely see her garden as a "large litter box" thanks to all the sand.

But in a follow-up video, Caity showed the end result of her beach club transformation, as she filmed herself sitting in her blow-up pool while riding an inflatable flamingo. She had friends over for a beach-themed party, including cocktails, bikinis, and plenty of beach-related decor.

While the sand might have been a bit of fail, the beach club vibe was definitely still there!

Man and dog found dead in van as 999 crews descend on Cornwall layby

Devon and Cornwall Police were called to a layby on the B3273, St Austell, at 3pm on Friday, May 1, following concerns raised about the vehicle.

Both the man and the dog were discovered dead inside the van, and the next of kin have since been informed.

Primark has quietly released a collection of pyjamas that has people who grew up in the 2000s feeling very nostalgic. It even caught the attention of a TV star who starred in the popular children's show that inspired the new range.

Based on the Jacqueline Wilson book, The Story of Tracy Beaker was adapted into a CBBC series in 2002. It ran until 2005 and produced various spin-offs as well as merchandise, which now includes a new Primark pyjama collection. Fans were quick to comment on the new collection appearing in Primark stores in the UK. ‌



The top comment on Liv's post is Tracy Beaker star Dani Harmer, who played the title character from 2002. She said: "Oh I am buying that entire collection!"

‌



In her own follow-up video ( @Daniharmer ), she asked: "Tracy Beaker pyjamas in Primark? What is going on? I need confirmation. Are these actually real?" She claimed that fans tagged her in clips "about 6,000 times", but some were convinced these videos are AI.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Fans of the show also piled into the comments section. One said: "Why are they not on click and collect? I'm having a meltdown!" Another put: "Oh bog off! Looks like I’m going to Primark!"

News.title: Hantavirus 'human-to-human strain' may have caused outbreak, expert warns
News.content:
Hantavirus 'human-to-human strain' may have caused outbreak, expert warns

World Health Organisation insists ‘no need to panic’ despite deaths of three aboard cruise ship linked to hantavirus - as scientists give their verdict

View 3 Images Experts are speculating on how rat virus could have spread between humans

Health chiefs have warned ‘there is no need to panic’ after three people died linked to a rat virus outbreak aboard a cruise ship.

‌



The World Health Organisation said travel restriction should not be implemented despite the outbreak of hantavirus which is usually spread via rodent droppings as experts debate how the victims could have contracted the virus. Two of the dead were a married couple, while a British man is in intensive care in South Africa.

‌



The outbreak was reported aboard the MV Hondius, travelling from Argentina to Cape Verde carrying 149 passengers and crew. The 69-year-old British man was evacuated to Johannesburg and is in a "critical but stable" condition having had a variant of hantavirus identified, Oceanwide Expeditions confirmed.

‌



MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak live: Brit fights for life in cruise ship horror READ MORE :

View 3 Images The MV Hondius has anchored off the coast of Cape Verde (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The three deaths are currently being investigated and hantavirus is suspected but lab tests are yet to confirm this. The first died aboard the ship on April 11 and the 70-year-old Dutch man was repatriated accompanied by his 69-year-old wife, who later fell ill and died. A third death of a German passenger occurred aboard the ship on Saturday.

Dr Michael Head, senior research fellow in global health at Southampton University, said: “When hearing about outbreaks on cruise ships, we tend to think of other diseases like Covid-19 or norovirus. Hantavirus is rarely associated with this setting, and person-to-person spread of the virus is also unusual.

‌



“Given the ship came from South America it’s plausible that the Andes strain of the virus may be responsible for this outbreak. There is previous reporting of person-to-person transmission from the Andes strain, though it’s not yet certain whether that’s the case here.”

The 353ft-long cruise ship, built in 2019, appears to have been stationary off the coast of Cape Verde for at least 24 hours.

Oceanwide Expeditions confirmed there are currently two crew members on board with acute respiratory symptoms, one mild and one severe. These crew members are of British and Dutch nationality and require urgent medical care. It added that no other persons with symptoms have currently been identified. There are 23 British national aboard, 19 of whom are passengers.

‌



View 3 Images People get hantavirus from contact with rodents like rats and mice (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Hantavirus refers to a strain of viruses carried by rats and mice transmitted to humans by inhaling particles from dried droppings. It can also spread through rodent bites or scratches but experts say human-to-human transmission is rare.

Dr Liam Brierley, of the MRC-University of Glasgow Centre for Virus Research, said: “Hantaviruses are transmitted to humans through breathing in virus in aerosol that has been shed from rodent droppings.

‌



“Importantly, hantaviruses are not transmissible from person to person except in extremely rare circumstances and only for one specific type of hantavirus called Andes virus, under very intensive close contact - such as between sexual partners or from hospital patient to hospital staff. It’s therefore extremely likely that these cases have resulted from the same single point of exposure to rodents.”

The virus can cause two severe illnesses which are Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) and Haemorrhagic Fever with Renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is often confused with the flu initially with symptoms such as fever and exhaustion but if respiratory symptoms develop then data suggests the fatality rate is as high as 38%. HFRS is even more severe and affects the kidneys, with symptoms including low blood pressure, internal bleeding, and then kidney failure.

Dr Hans Henri Kluge, regional director for WHO Europe, said: “We are acting with urgency to support the response to the hantavirus event on board a cruise vessel in the Atlantic, following the tragic loss of life. I thank the South African authorities for their rapid support, including care for a UK patient.

‌



“Hantavirus infections are uncommon and usually linked to exposure to infected rodents. While severe in some cases, it is not easily transmitted between people. The risk to the wider public remains low. There is no need for panic or travel restrictions.”

There is no treatment for hantavirus. Medics can usually only treat symptoms and support the body as the immune system attempts to fight off the infection. Treatments can include oxygen therapy, mechanical ventilation, antiviral medications and dialysis.

Dr Charlotte Hammer, Assistant Professor and infectious disease epidemiologist at Cambridge University, said: “It is not entirely uncommon for rodents to hitch a ride on a ship which would be one possibility, people having been infected when the ship last made port in Argentina is another possibility especially given that incubation periods of up to eight weeks.”

Article continues below

Prof Paul Hunter, leading expert in infectious diseases at the University of East Anglia, said: “Hantavirus is a viral infection that is acquired from contact with infected rodents. The virus is typically spread from rodents to humans through airborne aerosols of faeces and urine.

“There have been some suggestion that person-to-person spread may occur but there is still no agreement on this and others have concluded that evidence of person-to-person spread is not confirmed. If person-to-person spread happens at all it is rare. It is too early to speculate on how the affected people became infected but it is very unlikely that this outbreak would lead to an increased risk in the UK or elsewhere in Europe.”

News.title: Husband accused of brutally murdering Miss Switzerland finalist says he 'loved her'
News.content:
Husband accused of brutally murdering Miss Switzerland finalist says he 'loved her'

WARNING: DISTRESSING CONTENT A husband accused of murdering his beauty queen wife Kristina Joksimovic appeared in court and said he 'loved' her

View 3 Images Marc Rieben (r) appeared in court accused of murdering his wife Kristina Joksimovic (l) (Image: Kristina Joksimovic/Instagram)

A husband accused of murdering his wife, a former Miss Switzerland finalist and beauty queen, told a murder trial that he "loved" her.

Kristina Joksimovic's husband Marc Rieben, 43, has been accused of horrifically taking a knife, jigsaw tool and garden shears to his partner and hacking at her body. The man is also said to have "pureed" her remains in a blender.

Rieben appeared in court and the trial opened with the husband holding back tears as he claimed Kristina's death was "an accident" and he "loved" her with "all my heart". The father-of-two has been charged with murdering his then 38-year-old wife, in February 2024, and could face life behind bars if found guilty.

View 3 Images Kristina Joksimovic was killed and dismembered (Image: Kristina Joksimovic/Instagram)

The trial opened on Monday and Rieben appeared in court to open with a statement, in which he said he "loved" his wife but admitted to her "dying at my hands", as he held back tears. He said: "I have caused my family immeasurable suffering. Why? Why did I fail? Why couldn't I prevent it? Why couldn't I stop her from dying at my hands?

"I loved my wife with all my heart and believed in a future together. It haunts me day and night. What I did is absolutely unforgivable, and I take full responsibility. I deeply regret it, and I apologise."

The husband said leading up to his wife's horror death "the arguments were the main focus" but said people shouldn't forget "we had a passion", according to the Daily Mail. Rieben said he "admired" Kristina and her "entrepreneurial success and her ambitions" but revealed the pair, who had married in 2017, had been going to counselling since 2018.

View 3 Images Kristina Joksimovic died in February 2024 (Image: Kristina Joksimovic/Instagram)

The husband also revealed to the court that he paid his two children and Kristina's parents over £94,000. He said: "It would be wonderful if you could use it to do something that brings some lightness into your lives."

Rieben was then asked by the court why he offered that money today and not earlier, to which he replied: "Because this is the first opportunity I'll have to see the bereaved. This offer is made regardless of what the court decides. I simply want to show my support. It's a gesture."

Kristina was killed in the quiet village of in Binnigen, near Basel, and this trial, over two years on from her death, is expected to end on May 13. The mother's father discovered parts of her body at her home, after she failed to pick up her kids.

The indictment reportedly claims the motive for the shocking killing was Kristina asking for a divorce and her husband refusing. The indictment also reportedly claimed Rieben grabbed Kristina by the neck and shoved her against a wall while using a "ribbon-like" device around her neck.

Article continues below

Prosecutors claimed the man punched his wife while strangling her, adding she died an "agonising death". The document also claimed the man had acted "knowingly and intentionally, in full awareness and from a selfish attitude and mindset characterised by a need for control, resentment, revenge and massive anger".

Due to Switzerland's privacy laws, the victim and accused have been named as Thomas L and Ivana L in local media. The trial continues.

News.title: UK weather maps show sudden -3C freeze to hit this week - 8 coldest cities
News.content:
UK weather maps show sudden -3C freeze to hit this week - 8 coldest cities

Latest weather maps show the UK is expected to be hit by a cold snap on Wednesday, with parts of Scotland forecast to see temperature lows of -3C as Arctic air sweeps across the nation

View 4 Images The UK is braced for a cold spell (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Parts of Britain are set to endure freezing conditions within days, as fresh weather maps reveal temperatures nosediving to as low as -3C.

‌



According to the latest data, the bitter cold will sweep across the country at around 6am on Wednesday (May 6), following a spell of glorious sunshine.

‌



Today (Monday), some areas of the UK in and around London are enjoy temperatures hovering around 18C. But conditions will take a sharp turn for the worst from the early hours of Wednesday morning as the cold snap arrives.

‌



The latest weather charts from WXCharts indicate that Scotland will bear the brunt of the chill, with areas around Inverness facing temperature lows of -3C.

View 4 Images Weather maps show parts of the UK blasted by cold conditions (Image: WXCharts)

Major English cities will also see mercury dropping to single figures, according to the maps. Areas around Manchester and Birmingham will experience temperatures plummeting to 2C at around 6pm on Wednesday. London, Oxford, Gloucester and Norwich are expected to see lows of 6C, the maps suggest.

‌



The Met Office said: "Turning cooler for all as northerly winds set in across the UK. Some showers at times, though these lighter and fewer than the weekend with sunny spells emerging as well."

Nick Finnis, from Netweather.tv, wrote in his latest weather blog: "The new week will feature a cooler northerly flow to start the week, eventually veering northeasterly by mid-week, with a fair bit of cloud spreading down across the country in this flow - thick enough to bring scattered showers in places, though many places missing them and staying dry.

View 4 Images Several parts of the country will shiver in the cold, the maps suggest (Image: WXCharts)

‌



"Some bright or sunny spells will be likely in places too. After mid-week, wind looks to swing around to come from a southerly direction across the south eventually, as an area of low pressure moves down from the northwest, bringing in warmer air across the south.

"However, staying cooler across the north. Still a risk of showers in places after mid-week, more substantial rain in the far northwest on Thursday, though many places missing the showers, some places staying dry all week."

The weather expert noted that temperatures across the UK and much of northern and western Europe would fall below the seasonal average during the daytime on Wednesday.

‌



View 4 Images Cold air will impact many areas of the country (Image: WXCharts)

He added: "Wednesday looks like the coolest day of the week, as flow turns northeasterly, bringing arctic air in across the north. Could be quite cloudy across many areas, with limited spells of sunshine and some showers across northern and western areas. Temperatures 10-15C at best."

News.title: Travel company confirms 23 Brits on board MV Hondius cruise ship amid hantavirus outbreak
News.content:
Travel company confirms 23 Brits on board MV Hondius cruise ship amid hantavirus outbreak

There are 19 passengers from Great Britain and four British crew members trapped on a cruise ship off Cape Verde. Two Brits have so far been hit by the outbreak.

View 5 Images The MV Hondius stationary off the coast of Cape Verde just off the port of Praia have not been given permission to stop (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

There are 23 Brits on board the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly virus outbreak linked to three deaths, it has been revealed.

‌



There are now two Brits who have been struck down including a crew member after hantavirus was found on board the MV Hondius. Oceanwide Expedition say they are dealing with a 'serious medical situation' on board the MV Hondius and confirmed 19 passengers alongside four crew were from Great Britain.

‌



According to experts, the rat-borne virus could have been picked up before tourists set off on their dream cruise at the ‘End of the World’ in Argentina. Passengers have been suggesting on social media that the tourist first taken ill had been travelling in Patagonia before the cruise set off.

‌



View 5 Images Cruise operator Oceanwide Expeditions said it is managing 'a serious medical situation' (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

MV Hondius cruise ship operator breaks silence on fatal Hantavirus outbreak on board READ MORE :

A British tourist, aged 69, who was on the doomed MV Hondius trip to the Antarctic, is currently in intensive care in Johannesburg but described as 'critical but stable'. There are two crew members who are sick and still on board - one of them is also British.

Currently scared passengers are trapped on the ship as the port they were due to disembark at in Cape Verde has refused them entry. They have been told to wear face masks and keep their distance from other passengers.

‌



A medical team from Cape Verde in full protective gear was sent to the ship to see the sick crew members. But the president of the Cape Verdean Public Health Institute (INSP), Maria da Luz has said that the ship is in quarantine and should “continue its route” and said passengers will not be disembarking there in order to protect the local population, A Nacao reported.

It is now believed the ship will head for the Canary Islands. In a statement released on Monday Oceanwide Expeditions said they are still "dealing with a serious medical situation on board the m/v Hondius, which is currently off the coast of Cape Verde."

They supplied a list of passengers and crew saying there were a total of 88 passengers from around the world and 61 crew. Of those 23 were from Great Britain and two from Ireland. They also said one of the two crew members sick on board was from Great Britain.

‌



View 5 Images MV Hondius where three people have died from a suspected deadly virus caught from rodents. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

In a brief timeline of events they said it started on April 11 when "a passenger died on board" adding that "the cause of death could not be determined." They said in a statement: "On April 24, this passenger was disembarked on St Helena, with his wife accompanying the repatriation. On April 27, Oceanwide Expeditions was informed that the wife had become unwell during the return journey and had later died.

"Both passengers were Dutch nationals. At this time, it has not been confirmed that these two deaths are connected to the current medical situation on board. On 27 April, another passenger became seriously ill and was medically evacuated to South Africa. This person is currently being treated in the intensive care unit in Johannesburg and is in a critical but stable condition. This passenger is of British nationality. A variant of hantavirus has been identified in this patient.

‌



"On 2 May, another passenger on board died. The cause has not yet been established. This passenger was of German nationality. In addition, there are currently two crew members on board with acute respiratory symptoms, one mild and one severe. Both require urgent medical care. These crew members are of British and Dutch nationality. At this time, no other persons with symptoms have been identified."

The travel company stated that hantavirus "has not currently been confirmed" in the two people on board who require medical care, "not has it been established that the virus is connected to the three deaths associated with this voyage." The company added the cause and possible connections are being investigated and that "the only confirmed case of hantavirus is the passenger who was medically evacuated and is now being treated in Johannesburg."

The travel company confirmed that the ship is still docked off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board from 23 different countries. They added that local health authorities have visited and assessed the situation. Talking about next stepys, they said: "The option of sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife are being considered to be the gateway for disembarkation, where further medical screening and handling could take place.

‌



"Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported. Oceanwide Expeditions is in close contact with those directly involved and their families, and is providing support where possible."

Local reports in Argentina, where the ship set off from, suggest urgent inquiries are being made to find out where the tourists stayed before embarking on the 45-day cruise. The Patagonia region in Argentina has seen a Hantavirus outbreak spread by long-tailed rodents.

The deadly cases have been on the rise in more central areas, away from the port, but it is not known if the tourists took part in any trips inland before the sailaway. The numbers of cases in Argentina have been increasing in recent weeks with concerns about the fatality rate which reached 28 deaths last year. This year, in just two weeks, four people including a child under 10 died from hantavirus in Buenos Aires province.

‌



View 5 Images A long-tailed deer mouse has been linked to Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) which causes respiratory distress (Image: Getty Images)

Epidemiologist Michael Baker told the BBC passengers who had the suspected hantavirus would have been infected before they got on board the cruise ship due to the virus's long incubation period. He added that it was rare for humans to get the hantavirus and "very unusual" for people to develop the disease on a cruise ship. "That's the worst possible place to get seriously ill," Professor Baker says.

He says anyone with symptoms on board should be "rapidly evacuated" and taken to hospital with intensive care to increase their chances of survival. When asked what steps should be taken next, Professor Baker says the outbreak needs to be "investigated thoroughly" to see if there were any preventable factors, including traveller itineraries to see if they were exposed to high risk environments.

‌



La Nacion newspaper in Argentina said: “Authorities are investigating whether the initial infection occurred through environmental contact with rodents in rural areas before boarding, or if there was an outbreak within the ship's logistics." Quoting sources from the epidemiology department, it said: “We need information on whether the people were on tourist excursions in any area of Patagonia where it is found, or if it was present on the ship.”

The ship does offer day trips before sailing in the region including hiking to rural areas. A 70-year-old Dutch passenger was the first to show symptoms. He died on board, and his body was taken to Saint Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic. His wife, aged 69, was then also taken sick and flown to South Africa where she died in hospital.

The Brit became ill at Saint Helena and is now in intensive care in Johannesburg. Two crew members are sick on board with plans to move them, while a body remains on board. A spokesperson from the South African Department of Health says the British tourist "became ill while the ship was travelling from St Helena to Ascension Island, and was transferred from a hospital in Ascension to a South African private health facility in Sandton for medical attention".

‌



View 5 Images Inside the MV Hondius which was supposed to disembark on Cape Verde on Bank Holiday Monday (Image: Hondius)

It was hoped the two crew members would first get help on Cape Verde and would then be repatriated to the Netherlands along with the dead body still on board. Another passenger who was travelling with the deceased but who doesn’t have any symptoms will also be repatriated. In a statement the World Health Organisation said they were “aware of and supporting a public health event involving a cruise vessel sailing in the Atlantic Ocean.”

“To date, one case of hantavirus infection has been laboratory confirmed, and there are five additional suspected cases. Of the six affected individuals, three have died and one is currently in intensive care in South Africa. Detailed investigations are ongoing, including further laboratory testing…”

‌



They said Hantavirus infections are typically linked to exposure to infected rodents’ urine or faeces, adding: “While rare, hantavirus may spread between people, and can lead to severe respiratory illness and requires careful patient monitoring, support and response.”

WHO Regional Director for Europe, Dr Hans Henri P. Kluge said in a statement: “We are acting with urgency to support the response to the hantavirus event on board a cruise vessel in the Atlantic, following the tragic loss of life. WHO/Europe is working with the countries involved to support medical care, evacuation, investigations and public health risk assessment.

“I am in close contact with our teams to ensure a coordinated, science-based response. I thank the South African authorities for their rapid support, including care for a UK patient. Hantavirus infections are uncommon and usually linked to exposure to infected rodents. While severe in some cases, it is not easily transmitted between people.

Article continues below

“The risk to the wider public remains low. There is no need for panic or travel restrictions. Having just returned from the African continent, where I discussed closer collaboration on health emergencies, this is a timely reminder: health threats do not respect borders. Working together is how we protect people.”

The ship left the port of Ushuaia,in Patagonia, Argentina, known as the ‘The End of the World’ at South America’s southern tip on March 20 for the 45 day trip. It sailed the Beagle Channel, described as a “thrilling gateway to Patagonia and Antarctica” stopping at South Georgia, Tristan do Cunha, Saint Helena and the Ascension Islands.

It was due to disembark in Cape Verde on Sunday but permission was withheld for the ship, which can hold 170 passengers. Hantavirus is transmitted through rodents, particularly through contact with their urine, feces, and saliva, according to the US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

News.title: 'I'm an American in London and 1 thing changes about British people on bank holidays'
News.content:
'I'm an American in London and 1 thing changes about British people on bank holidays'

Many people are enjoying an extra day off work today because it's a bank holiday - and one American man, who's currently in London, has noticed a major change about Brits on a bank holiday weekend

View Image An American in London has noticed a significant shift in British people this bank holiday (stock image) (Image: Henry Nicholls/AFP via Getty Images)

An American man currently in the UK has spotted one significant change about British people when a bank holiday hits. May offers two bank holidays for people to enjoy - one at the start of the month and another coming towards the end of the month.

‌



Bank holidays are a calendar highlight, seeing banks, businesses and schools shut up shop and giving workers - and children - an extra day off. They’re designated under the Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971, or by Royal Proclamation.

‌



Typically, they fall on a Monday which results in a long weekend, with eight days in total throughout 2026 in England and Wales, nine in Scotland and 10 in Northern Ireland. They’re a popular feature of UK life - after all, who doesn’t love an extra day off from work?

‌



One American man, who posts online under the name Kjordy, creates content on social media centered on his travel adventures. In a recent video posted on Instagram, he detailed the joys of a bank holiday weekend - and how much happier everyone seemed to be.

Kjordy filmed himself walking through London, the bright blue sky in the background, and spoke directly to the camera.

He began: “I don’t know what it is about a bank holiday but London is a different vibe right now. For my Americans that don’t know, a couple times a year, you get a Monday off so the Friday before, everyone’s in such a good mood because they get one more day of freedom.”

‌



Kjordy then went on to describe the happiness emanating from British people this bank holiday weekend. He said: “And today is just hitting different.

“I mean, I think it helps that it’s probably like 24 degrees - it’s the first time we saw the sun in Lord knows how long - but they are happy.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



“I don’t think y’all are deep in this; people are walking around with a smile on their face. I can’t tell you the last time I saw a random stranger smile at me. A granny blew a kiss at me, I kid you not, a granny blew a kiss at me.

“Today’s gonna be a good day. I’m seeing people drinking Aperol Spritz outside of places and [carrying] ice bags walking down Clapham Common. You know it’s a vibe, man.”

He added: “I don’t know about y’all but I’m gonna have the disco bumping this weekend. I’m about to hop on the tube but I really think this is the mood boost that London needed, bro.”

‌



The camera then cut to a man asking to take a photo with him. Over the top of the footage, Kjordy added text which simply read “sees a guy off camera looking joyous” to provide context to the interaction. He branded the man “one of the nicest guys ever”.

In the comments section, fellow Instagram users were keen to share their thoughts, with many agreeing the bank holiday weekend promoted a definite shift in people’s moods.

One person said: “Canadian living in London and it's my first summer bank holiday and I love it!!!!”

Article continues below

Another joked: “England is the most bipolar country I swear” while a third said: “Vibes are unmatched when the sun’s out in London”.

A fourth added: “I love this analysis, it’s basically stuff we Brits already know but just hearing you telling us what we already know is a gift”.

News.title: Temperatures to fall this week after the bank holiday
News.content:
After last week's warmth, the first full week of May is set to see temperatures tumble across the UK.

Temperatures peaked around 25C (77F) in parts of England on Friday, but this week is shaping up to be noticeably cooler.

There is a mixed forecast for this May Bank Holiday.

Scotland started on a frosty note before a passing weather front is set to bring rain to the far north. But the picture is much brighter elsewhere, feeling springlike and pleasantly warm in the sunshine thanks to the strengthening May sun.

Northern Ireland will fare well through the day, staying mostly dry with warm sunny spells.

In England and Wales, where the early patchy fog cleared quickly, cloudier skies are expected to dominate into the afternoon. Where the cloud breaks and sunshine develops across northern parts of England and Wales, it should make it feel warmer than Sunday.

Further south, however, sunshine will be more limited, and there is a greater chance of lively showers developing, with the possibility of an isolated rumble of thunder.

News.title: Police airlift crocodile from river on suspicion of eating missing businessman
News.content:
A crocodile has been helicoptered out of a river in South Africa after police suspected it of eating a missing person.

The ‘highly dangerous and complex’ operation came at the end of a week-long search for businessman Gabriel Batista, 59, who had been reported missing after his car became trapped in floodwaters.

Aerial reconnaissance had identified the reptile after it appeared unusually still, with a full, distended gut - a sign it had recently eaten a large meal.

The huge alligator, which was shot dead before being moved, was airlifted from the Komati River by a police diving team and delivered to Kruger National Park, where human remains were found in its stomach.

A South African Police Services statement confirmed the remains would be sent for DNA testing to confirm the identity of the victim.

Several varieties of frozen pizzas sold at Aldi and Walmart have been recalled due to a potential salmonella contamination.

On Thursday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service issued a public health alert for meat and poultry products that contain FDA-regulated ingredients formulated with dry milk powder.

The dairy-based product, which the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now recalled, could have been contaminated with salmonella, a bacterium that causes food poisoning.

open image in gallery The recall included three of Great Value’s frozen pizzas, sold at Walmart stores nationwide ( U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service )

Six products with the affected dry milk powder have been recalled, including Mama Cozzi’s Biscuit Crust Sausage & Cheese Breakfast Pizza and another called Biscuit Crust Cooked Pork Belly Crumbles, Cooked Bacon Topping, Pepper & Onion Breakfast Pizza. They were both sold at Aldi stores nationwide.

The recall also includes three Great Value frozen pizzas: Thin Crust Chicken Bacon Ranch, Ultra Thin Crust Chicken Bacon Ranch and Stuffed Crust Chicken Bacon Ranch — all sold at Walmart stores across the country.

open image in gallery The frozen pizzas contained a dry milk powder that may have been contaminated with salmonella ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

In addition, Culinary Circle’s Ultra Thin Crust Chicken Bacon Ranch frozen pizza and Pork King’s Sour Cream & Onion Pork Rinds and Party Size Sour Cream & Onion Pork Rinds have been recalled.

In its announcement, the food safety agency said there’s “no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption” of these pizzas or pork rinds. However, the agency is urging consumers to throw the products away immediately or return them where they bought them for a full refund.

Recalled items can be identified with their production dates, Best By dates, lot codes and establishment numbers, found here. The agency says it expects to identify and recall additional products made with the dry milk powder.

open image in gallery The recall includes two Mama Cozzi’s pizzas, sold at Aldi’s stores nationwide ( U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service )

People suffering from salmonella infections can develop symptoms within 12 to 72 hours after eating contaminated food, according to the FDA. Symptoms — which last from four to seven days and usually go away without treatment — can include diarrhea, fever and abdominal cramps. People with severe infections can experience high fever, headaches, lethargy, a rash or blood in the urine or stool.

In recent months, several food products have been recalled due to concerns about potential salmonella infections. Last week, Ghirardelli recalled dozens of its hot cocoa and frappe mixes over concerns that its milk powder was contaminated with salmonella. However, in a statement, the chocolate company said it was issuing the recall “out of an abundance of caution,” and that no illnesses were reported.

In March, Costco recalled its Meatloaf with Mashed Yukon Potatoes and Glaze because an ingredient in it was potentially contaminated with salmonella.

The affected meatloaf products had sell-by dates between March 5 and March 16, 2026. Recalled meals were sold at Costco stores between March 2 and March 13 in 26 states.

Foreclosure rates shot up at the start of 2026 but experts say the trend isn’t worrisome… yet.

Some 118,727 properties were in foreclosure nationwide during the first three months of 2026 - up 26 percent from a year ago and the highest number since 2020, a recent report from housing data and analytics firm ATTOM revealed.

States with the highest foreclosure rate - number of homes in foreclosure versus total number of homes - were Indiana (1 in 739), followed by South Carolina (1 in 743), Florida (1 in 750), Delaware (1 in 757) and Illinois (1 in 833), according to the report.

For cities with at least 200,000 people, the South was hit hardest. Two Florida cities, Lakeland and Punta Gorda, had the two highest foreclosure rates in the country, followed by Columbia, South Carolina; Fayetteville, North Carolina; and Macon, Georgia, ATTOM reported.

Foreclosure starts - the number of homes that began the process at a given time, were up 20 percent from a year ago.

open image in gallery Some 118,727 properties were in foreclosure during the first three months of 2026 - up 26 percent from a year ago and the highest number since 2020 ( Getty Images )

Responses to the data were mixed. Some - like ATTOM CEO Rob Barber - believe that the numbers indicate that Americans are feeling the pressure of higher prices across the board and may struggle to pay their mortgages.

There’s certainly evidence for that in the current economy. Mortgage rates have remained above 6 percent since September 2022 after staying under 6 percent for around 13 years. Inflation has driven up the cost of goods past the Federal Reserve’s 2-percent target rate for just over five years. Average housing prices remain near historic highs, according to data from the Federal Reserve.

These factors and others have put tremendous strain on consumer finances, so much so that Americans are more fearful for their finances now than they were during the 2008 Great Recession.

However, others say the spike is more of a return to normal foreclosure rates after five years of suppressed figures thanks to pandemic-era homeowner protections.

That was the opinion of Donna Schmidt, CEO of DLS Servicing, a company that helps mortgage lenders make the foreclosure and repossession process more efficient. Schmidt told housing market publication HousingWire that five years of putting off foreclosures could result in a rush in the next two years.

open image in gallery Americans are more fearful for their finances now than they were during the 2008 Great Recession ( AFP/Getty )

If foreclosure rates remain the same through the first half of the year, there would be roughly 60,000 fewer than the first six months of 2019, according to data from ATTOM.

As Americans have struggled to make ends meet, President Donald Trump has suggested two ways to make homeownership more affordable.

Trump floated the idea of a 50-year mortgage, which would lower monthly payments. He also signed an executive order banning Wall Street investors from buying single family homes, a move that was meant to free up inventory and, in theory, lower home prices. In both cases, experts expressed skepticism over their long-term effectiveness.

News.title: Hearts v Rangers LIVE: Team news and updates as Scottish Premiership title rivals meet at Tynecastle
News.content:
Hearts take a four-point lead over Rangers into a massive Premiership title clash at Tynecastle ( PA )

Hearts face another huge test of their Premiership title credentials as they face Rangers at Tynecastle.

The leaders are four games away from a first league title since 1960 and breaking the Old Firm’s stranglehold of the Scottish top-flight. Hearts negotiated nine-man Hibs last weekend and could go three points clear of Celtic with three games to go with a win today.

Rangers are in “must-win” territory now having lost to Motherwell at Ibrox last weekend; lose at Tynecastle and Danny Rohl’s side will be seven points off the pace and surely out of the running.

Derek McInnes insisted his Hearts side were still “underdogs” in the title race but the Jambos have performed well against the Old Firm clubs this season and have already beaten Rangers and Celtic twice each.

Another three points would take Hearts a step closer to a history title and one of the biggest shocks Scottish football has produced.

I didn’t understand leeks when I was growing up; in fact, I never ate them. It took living in France for me to fall for them.

This Leek Quiche recipe, from my cookbook “V Is for Vegetables,” was not only the first thing I learned in cooking school in Paris; it was also part of my final “exam.” I had to make it under the close scrutiny of the chefs. So you’d better believe I take leeks seriously.

Leeks are the mildest of the indispensable onion family, less pungent than garlic and shallots, richer and more discreet when cooked. We do not eat them raw, but they soften quickly, and as they warm, their deliciousness is revealed. Leeks are easy to use. Make sure to wash them thoroughly (soil lodges in their tight layers).

This quiche has three distinctive components: the dough, the filling and the egg mixture, good things to perfect! It's delicious for breakfast and lunch at home with any number of filling variations: mushrooms, spinach, onions and so on. The tart comes together pretty quickly if you make the dough in advance. You’ll only need the white and pale green leek parts for the quiche, so save the dark greens for stock.

Leek Quiche

Servings: 1 (10-inch) quiche

Ingredients

TART DOUGH

1 ¾ cups flour

1 teaspoon salt

9 tablespoons butter, cubed and chilled

1 egg yolk

Up to 4 tablespoons ice water

FILLING

4 tablespoons (½ stick) butter, plus more for the pan

3 large leeks (white and pale green parts), diced

1 large clove garlic, minced

Salt and pepper

Small handful fresh flat-leaf parsley, chopped

Flour (for the pan and rolling the dough)

½ cup whole milk

½ cup heavy cream

2 eggs

1 egg yolk

Pinch grated nutmeg

Salt and pepper

¾ cup grated Parmigiano

Directions

Stir together the flour and salt in a large bowl. Add the butter and, little by little, work it into the flour with your fingertips, flattening it to create a sandy mixture. The idea is not to overwork the dough and the key is to start with cold butter and touch it with only your fingertips.

Add the yolk and 2 tablespoons of the ice water, then lightly stir and fold it in with your fingers.

Do not worry if the mixture seems too dry and like it won’t come together. Just add more water, drop by drop, until it does.

When the mixture just barely becomes a dough, transfer to a bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for about an hour.

Preheat the oven to 350°F. Heat the 4 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Sweat the leeks and garlic with salt and pepper until soft, about 10 minutes. Take off the heat and stir in the parsley, then set the leek mixture aside to cool.

Meanwhile, butter and flour a 10-inch tart pan with a removable bottom, then set it on a baking sheet. Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 1/8 inch thick. Fit the dough into the tart pan, trim off any excess, and poke the bottom with a fork in several places to let air escape and help the dough keep its shape while cooking.

Line the tart shell with a circle of parchment paper and fill with dried chickpeas, beans, or pie weights. Bake for about 25 minutes, then remove the parchment and beans and bake until the crust is golden and cooked through, another 10 minutes.

When the tart shell is ready, whisk together the milk, cream, eggs, yolk, nutmeg, and 2 pinches each of salt and pepper. Spread the leek mixture evenly in the shell, then gently pour in the milk mixture, leaving the top of the crust exposed. Do not overfill! Top with the cheese and bake until the filling is set and golden brown, about 30 minutes. Let it sit for 10 minutes before serving.

—-

Michael Anthony is the executive chef-partner of Gramercy Tavern, chef-partner of Lex Yard at the Waldorf Astoria, and the author of “The Gramercy Tavern Cookbook.” He has received several James Beard Awards including Best Chef in New York City, Outstanding Chef, and a James Beard Book Award for his cookbook “V Is for Vegetables.” Prior to joining Gramercy Tavern in 2006, he was the executive chef of Blue Hill at Stone Barns.
